title: Tariffs Are Back, Apple’s Big Bet, and AI’s Real Impact - The Friday Market Wrap!
summary: Eisman distinguishes headline tariffs from effective rates, questions Apple spending promises, and surveys AI beneficiaries and potential victims. Gartner is his early example of AI threatening an incumbent information business. The wrap also contrasts current biotech earnings with pipeline news and reiterates skepticism about Opendoor.
assessment: The most consequential uncertainty is causal: Gartner weakness does not yet prove free AI substitution. Apple skepticism uses an inconsistent spending comparison because its US commitment includes suppliers, employees and content as well as physical investment. The pipeline discussion is useful if clinical outcomes are separated from investor expectations.
framework_points: Calculate effective policy exposure after exemptions.
Read the definition behind a large investment announcement.
Distinguish proprietary economics from commodity hardware.
Separate pipeline value from current earnings.
Look for both winners and threatened incumbents in AI.
transcript_cautions: Palantir tenfold growth is a reported CEO aspiration, not Eisman own target.
Apple US spending and China manufacturing investment are not automatically comparable categories.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: Effective tariffs may be 13%-14% overall, with much lower Canada and Mexico rates after exemptions.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton, reported by Steve Eisman
claims.test: Rebuild customs collections divided by covered imports using the same period and exemptions.
claims.reason: The quoted guest estimates require import weights, compliance rates and a defined collection period. Headline tariff schedules alone cannot verify them.
claims.next_check: Rebuild customs collections divided by covered imports using the same period and exemptions.

claims.claim: USMCA exemptions give Canada and Mexico a relative advantage that may attract North American supply chains.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Apply product-level origin rules and compare landed costs and realized relocation.
claims.reason: Specified tariff exemptions are real, but sectoral duties remain and the supply-chain forecast needs actual investment evidence.

evidence.title: 2025 tariff requirements
evidence.finding: USMCA origin rules provide exemptions from specified tariffs, while sectoral Section 232 duties and other rules must be evaluated separately.

claims.next_check: Apply product-level origin rules and compare landed costs and realized relocation.

claims.claim: Brazil and India may face harsher tariffs partly because they promote alternatives to the dollar.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Look for documented decision rationale rather than infer intent from tariff levels.
claims.reason: This is an explicitly tentative motive claim with no direct primary evidence isolating that cause.
claims.next_check: Look for documented decision rationale rather than infer intent from tariff levels.

claims.claim: Apple $600 billion US commitment is hard to believe because physical annual investment would exceed its China investment.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use matched spending definitions and audit actual incremental four-year delivery.
claims.reason: Skepticism about incremental delivery is reasonable, but the US spending definition includes supplier purchases, employment and content. Comparing it with physical manufacturing investment overstates the apparent inconsistency.

evidence.title: Scope of Apple US spending commitment
evidence.finding: The original spending package included supplier purchases, direct employment, infrastructure, facilities and content production, rather than only new physical factory investment.

evidence.title: Expanded US investment commitment
evidence.finding: Apple increased the four-year commitment to $600 billion, including supplier and manufacturing partnerships. Completion of the four-year commitment is not yet observable.

claims.next_check: Use matched spending definitions and audit actual incremental four-year delivery.

claims.claim: Palantir is growing rapidly, but classified government work limits outside diligence.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile disclosed government and commercial revenue with available procurement data.
claims.reason: Confidentiality constrains customer detail, yet public procurement and financial disclosures can still provide evidence. The absolute limits require contract-level analysis.
claims.next_check: Reconcile disclosed government and commercial revenue with available procurement data.

claims.claim: Palantir could grow tenfold over five years.
claims.speaker: Alex Karp, reported by Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define the metric and compare the five-year outcome with the original base.
claims.reason: This is a reported CEO aspiration with a 2030 endpoint, not Eisman adoption of a numerical target.
claims.next_check: Define the metric and compare the five-year outcome with the original base.

claims.claim: Caterpillar should benefit if factory expensing creates a construction boom, but current results do not yet show it.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track construction activity, orders and margins against the policy implementation dates.
claims.reason: The conditional mechanism lacks a defined boom threshold and return horizon. Eligibility and tax saving should not be equated with every factory being free.
claims.next_check: Track construction activity, orders and margins against the policy implementation dates.

claims.claim: Apollo private-lending growth and fee earnings can offset private-equity exit-market weakness.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile inflows and earnings by lending, insurance and equity strategy.
claims.reason: The business-mix distinction is meaningful, but fee-related growth, spread income, realizations and fund liquidity must be assessed separately.
claims.next_check: Reconcile inflows and earnings by lending, insurance and equity strategy.

claims.claim: Biotech pipeline setbacks can outweigh good current revenue and earnings, as Vertex demonstrates.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate current cash flows from probability-weighted pipeline value.
claims.reason: The VX-993 decision provides a concrete adverse pipeline development. It does not mean all Vertex pain research stopped or all clinical endpoints failed.

evidence.title: VX-993 phase 2 acute-pain results
evidence.finding: Vertex did not advance VX-993 monotherapy in acute pain after the study. This does not mean all its pain programs were discontinued.

claims.next_check: Separate current cash flows from probability-weighted pipeline value.

claims.claim: Eaton and Vertiv benefit from data-center demand, but high valuations make disappointing guidance costly.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare data-center orders, margins, backlog conversion and implied growth.
claims.reason: The exposure thesis is plausible, but the exact revenue shares and causal price reaction need segment disclosures and dated expectations.
claims.next_check: Compare data-center orders, margins, backlog conversion and implied growth.

claims.claim: Gartner weaker demand reflects government cutbacks and possibly substitution by free AI information.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track client retention, contract value, procurement cuts and documented reasons for cancellations.
claims.reason: Weaker growth is observable; the AI substitution explanation remains a hypothesis. Its own AI product and other demand drivers complicate causal attribution.

evidence.title: Gartner Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Results showed weaker contract-value growth and a reduced revenue outlook. The issuer also described its AskGartner product; these disclosures do not isolate customer substitution by free AI.

claims.next_check: Track client retention, contract value, procurement cuts and documented reasons for cancellations.

claims.claim: Gartner may foreshadow a painful adjustment for consulting and some software companies.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare exposed businesses and control groups using revenue, retention and pricing.
claims.reason: The forward warning has no sector basket, magnitude or deadline, and the starting causal premise remains unproven.
claims.next_check: Compare exposed businesses and control groups using revenue, retention and pricing.

claims.claim: AMD data-center results show it is not yet catching up with Nvidia.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare accelerator-only revenue, deployments and customer economics.
claims.reason: Catching up needs a shared market metric and period; different products, export restrictions and CPU revenue can distort aggregate comparisons.
claims.next_check: Compare accelerator-only revenue, deployments and customer economics.

claims.claim: Supermicro has weaker proprietary economics and an impaired reporting reputation relative to leading AI platforms.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare gross margins, differentiation, switching costs and reporting controls.
claims.reason: The competitive distinction is plausible, but product differentiation, customer concentration and audited accounting history require separate tests.
claims.next_check: Compare gross margins, differentiation, switching costs and reporting controls.

claims.claim: Arista is a more differentiated beneficiary of data-center growth than commodity server assemblers.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare software integration, switching costs, margins and customer concentration.
claims.reason: This is a comparative business-quality view without an investment horizon or valuation rule. Strong growth alone does not prove permanent protection.
claims.next_check: Compare software integration, switching costs, margins and customer concentration.

claims.claim: Rockwell and Emerson soft guidance shows the expected tax-driven industrial boom has not yet arrived.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track new orders and realized capex after eligibility dates.
claims.reason: A near-term reporting lag is plausible, but the specific policy contribution cannot be isolated from underlying automation demand and project timing.
claims.next_check: Track new orders and realized capex after eligibility dates.

claims.claim: Disney legacy television decline limits the benefit of growing parks and streaming.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare segment revenue, operating profit and required reinvestment.
claims.reason: A segment profit and capital-allocation bridge is needed to quantify how much the legacy drag offsets newer businesses.
claims.next_check: Compare segment revenue, operating profit and required reinvestment.

claims.claim: Shopify has regained stronger growth after the post-pandemic slowdown.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare merchant volume, take rate, recurring revenue and free cash flow.
claims.reason: The historical phase comparison needs consistent organic metrics and treatment of exited logistics operations; a share-price recovery alone is insufficient.
claims.next_check: Compare merchant volume, take rate, recurring revenue and free cash flow.

claims.claim: Lilly trial results can be clinically successful yet disappoint investors expecting greater weight loss.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Keep trial population, estimand, dose and expectations separate.
claims.reason: The trial met its primary endpoint and produced 12.4% efficacy-estimand loss at the highest dose. That clinical result is distinct from a market expectation for 15% or more.

evidence.title: ATTAIN-1 topline results
evidence.finding: At the highest dose, efficacy-estimand weight loss averaged 12.4% at 72 weeks in the specified trial population. The trial met its primary endpoint; a stock-market disappointment is not a failed clinical endpoint.

claims.next_check: Keep trial population, estimand, dose and expectations separate.

claims.claim: Opendoor weak housing outlook and capital-intensive model make its meme valuation hard to justify.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track holding periods, contribution profit, cash use and dilution.
claims.reason: The critique needs inventory economics, financing and a valuation model. A one-week share decline does not by itself settle a long-term business thesis.
claims.next_check: Track holding periods, contribution profit, cash use and dilution.

claims.claim: Venture capital remains bifurcated after the 2022 downturn, and stale accounting can hide weak fund economics.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare distributions, realizations, marks and fundraising by vintage and sector.
claims.reason: The adopted guest explanation needs fund-vintage cash flows and realization evidence. Broad statements about most opportunities being only AI or crypto lack a measurable universe.
claims.next_check: Compare distributions, realizations, marks and fundraising by vintage and sector.
